description: How the import pipeline (js/scripts/import-native-grammars.mjs) turns the rule names of an upstream grammar into readable English native rule names and concept records: the abbreviations and run-together keywords upstream names use with the words that replace them, and per grammar the names and concepts a reviewer decided by hand. Every entry is a reviewed merge decision; the merge report of each language lists where it applied.

conflicts.reason: Theorem Proving in Lean 4 section 2.9 (Implicit Arguments) checks `@foo`, the function with all its arguments made explicit (`#check @ident`, `#check @List.cons`); tree-sitter-lean4 0.3.0 reduces the command before an `@`, which may open the attributes of a next declaration (`@[simp] def`), and recovers from it. The merged grammar keeps both parses there: the attributes need the `[` that follows, the explicit term does not.

grammar.type-assertion.reason: A type assertion <T>x tells the type checker to treat an expression as a type, while a case statement is one branch of a switch statement.

grammar.function-declaration.reason: A function declaration binds a name to a function, while a use declaration brings the paths of another module into scope.

grammar.preprocessor-argument.reason: A preprocessor argument is the text after a directive or a macro name, while the preprocessor parameters are the names a function-like macro declares.

grammar.argument-list.reason: An argument list gives the values a call passes, while a parameter list declares the names a function takes.

grammar.condition.reason: A condition is the expression an if or while expression tests, while a term is an operand of addition or subtraction.

grammar.pattern.reason: A pattern matches and destructures a value in a program, while a grammar rule binds a non-terminal to an expression.

grammar.reference-expression.reason: A reference expression borrows a place with & or &mut, while an extension expression marks a GNU C extension with __extension__.

grammar.token-pattern.reason: A token pattern is the matcher of a macro rule, while a token rule is a grammar rule matched as one lexical token.

grammar.tokens.reason: Tokens are the token trees a macro rule expands to, while an item is one element of a list.

grammar.type.reason: A type classifies the values of an expression, while a character is one Unicode scalar value.

grammar.yield-expression.reason: A yield expression hands one value out of a generator and resumes after it, while a return expression leaves the function.

grammar.type-argument-list.reason: A type argument list gives the types a generic use supplies, while a type parameter list declares the names a generic item takes.

grammar.command.reason: A Lean command is one top-level declaration or directive of a module, which the elaborator reads in order, while a statement is one step of a block that runs in order.

grammar.syntax-quotation.reason: A Lean syntax quotation `(…) builds the syntax tree of the Lean source between its parentheses, while a syntax quote is a hash-apostrophe before a datum, which reads as a syntax form.

grammar.yield-statement.reason: A Java yield statement gives the value of the switch expression it ends, while a return statement ends a function and gives its result.

grammar.annotation.reason: A Java annotation attaches metadata to a declaration or a type (The Java Language Specification, section 9.7), while a notation declares new syntax for terms.

grammar.catch-type.reason: A Java catch type names the exception types a catch clause handles, while a match case is one branch of a match expression.

grammar.variadic-argument.reason: A Go variadic argument xs... passes the elements of a slice as the final arguments of a call, while a variadic parameter declares the final parameter that takes any number of them.

grammar.statement-list.reason: A Go statement list is the statements of a block or a case clause in order, while an argument list gives the values a call passes.

grammar.map-type.reason: A Go map type map[K]V is the type of the hash tables from keys of K to values of V, while a function type is the type of the functions with given parameters and results.

grammar.default-case.reason: A Go default case is the branch of a switch or select statement taken when no other case matches, while a default type is the type a TypeScript type parameter takes when none is given.

grammar.dependent-type.reason: The pinned source grammar defines dependent type and qualified type as separate productions with distinct literal spellings or contexts. Their grammar meanings retain those source distinctions; the WordNet synonym uses a different lexical sense.
